d: How connected agents delegate work to each other, and how Maestro Mode lets one agent assemble a team.
x: Talking through ropes # Connect two terminals and each becomes visible to the other. From inside a terminal: omaestri list # who and what is connected to me omaestri ask "Reviewer" "Review my PR" # send a prompt and wait for the reply omaestri check "Builder" # read the other agent's current screen ask types the prompt into the target terminal, waits until the agent goes idle, and prints what it answered. If your tool's timeout expires first, do not send the prompt again: use check to see progress, then wait. check reads the target's output without interrupting it. An optional line count limits it: omaestri check "Builder" 40 . list prints the terminals, notes and portals connected to the caller. Always run it first to get the exact names. Connections are the access control. A terminal that is not connected to another cannot ask or check it. Notes as shared memory # A note connected to a terminal is readable and writable by that agent: omaestri note create "initial content" # new note, linked to this terminal omaestri note read "Spec" # whole note omaestri note read "Spec" 10 20 # 20 lines starting at line 10 omaestri note write "Spec" "new content" # replace everything omaestri note edit "Spec" "old text" "new text" # replace a substring Portals # Agents can drive a connected browser portal: navigate, take a snapshot of the page structure with element references ( @e1 ), click, fill forms, press keys, scroll, take screenshots and evaluate JavaScript. See Portal commands . Maestro Mode # Maestro Mode turns a terminal into a lead that can build its own team. Enable it with the Maestro toggle when you create the terminal (or edit it later). A Maestro terminal can: Command Effect omaestri recruit "Name" --preset "Claude Code" --role "Reviewer" Create a new agent terminal o

d: The infinite canvas, the node types you can place on it and how to move around.
x: The canvas is an infinite 2D surface. Everything you work with is a node placed on it, and nodes can be joined by ropes . Node types # Node What it is Create it with Terminal A shell or an AI agent running in a VTE terminal. T , Ctrl + N , or the toolbar Note A Markdown sticky note with a raw and a formatted view. It can also point to an existing file. Toolbar, or drop a text file on the canvas File Tree A folder browser with Git badges. Dropping other files on the canvas (images, PDFs, video) opens them in a read-only portal. Every node has a header with its icon and title, a close button, and can be moved, resized and locked. A title can be renamed in place. Terminal names are unique within a workspace; see Terminals and agents . Ropes (connections) # A rope links two nodes. Ropes are drawn with a physics simulation and settle after you move a node. Ropes also carry permissions : a terminal can only see and address the terminals, notes and portals it is connected to. Select a node and press L to start a connection, then click the target. A terminal can be connected to another terminal, a note, or a portal. Notes and portals can also be linked to each other. d: Every omaestri command, grouped by what it does.
x: omaestri is injected into every terminal Maestrix creates. maestrix-cli and open-maestri are aliases. If omaestri is not on PATH (a shell that resets it), use "$MAESTRI_CLI" . Run omaestri help for the built-in summary and omaestri debug to diagnose a broken setup. Names are case-sensitive here: run omaestri list first and copy the exact name. Discovering and talking # Command Description omaestri list Terminals, notes and portals connected to the caller. omaestri ask "Agent" "prompt" Send a prompt and wait for the reply (the agent going idle). omaestri check "Agent" [lines] Read the agent's current screen without interrupting it. Notes # Command Description omaestri note create ["content"] Create a note linked and connected to this terminal. omaestri note read "Note" [offset limit] Read a note, or limit lines from line offset . omaestri note write "Note" "content" Replace the whole note. omaestri note edit "Note" "old" "new" Replace a substring in place. Portals # All portal commands need the portal name. @e1 style references come from snapshot . Command Description omaestri portal create "URL" ["Name"] Open a new portal. omaestri portal navigate "Portal" "URL" Go to a URL ( edit --url also works). omaestri portal info / snapshot / screenshot / html "Portal" Inspect the page. snapshot lists elements with references. omaestri portal text "Portal" @e1 Text of an element. omaestri portal click "Portal" @e1 Click by reference, CSS selector or "x,y" . omaestri portal fill "Portal" @e1 "value" Fill an input. omaestri portal type "Portal" "text" / key "Portal" "Enter" Type text or press a key. omaestri portal hover / scroll / drag / wait / evaluate … Hover, scroll ( down [amount] ), drag @e1 @e2 , wait for an element, run JavaScript. d: The processes behind Maestrix, who owns what, and how agents reach each other.
h: How the interface finds the server
x: The three parts # ┌──────────────────────────────┐ ┌────────────────────────────────────┐ │ GTK 4 + Cairo interface │ REST │ Swift server │ │ canvas, ropes, terminals │◄──────►│ workspaces, terminals (PTY), │ │ (VTE), notes, files, │ WS │ connections, floors, routines, │ │ portals (WebKitGTK) │ │ SSH │ └──────────────────────────────┘ └──────────────┬─────────────────────┘ │ Unix socket + HTTP ▼ ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐ │ omaestri (CLI) inside each │ │ terminal: list · ask · check · … │ └─────────────────────────────────────┘ Part Technology Responsibility Interface Python, GTK 4, Cairo, VTE, WebKitGTK Draws the canvas and ropes, shows terminals, notes, files and portals, runs dialogs and preferences. Server Swift ( open-maestri-server ) Owns shells (PTYs), stores workspaces, applies connection permissions, runs floors, routines and SSH. CLI Swift ( omaestri ) Runs inside terminals. Sends commands to the server, which routes them to other terminals. The server owns the shells # A terminal on the canvas is a view of a PTY that belongs to the server . The interface connects to it over a WebSocket and the server replays the saved screen on every connection. Consequences: Switching workspaces, or closing and reopening the window, does not kill a running shell or an agent. Terminal history survives restarts of the interface. If the server itself restarts, shells are gone. Maestrix then relaunches agents on their last conversation. See Terminals and agents . How the interface finds the server # The server binds a dynamic port and writes it to ~/.open-maestri/run/server.port . The interface reads that file, and re-reads it when the connection drops. While connected, the interface checks the server every few seconds; two misses in a row switch it to Standalone mo

d: The data directory, the files Maestrix writes, preferences and environment variables.
x: Data directory # Everything lives in ~/.open-maestri , or in the folder named by OPEN_MAESTRI_DATA_DIR when that variable is set. ~/.open-maestri/ ├── manifest.json # index of workspaces ├── sidebar-layout.json # groups and order of the sidebar ├── preferences.json # your preferences (see below) ├── app-state.json # includes the cleanShutdown flag used for crash recovery ├── routines.json # scheduled routines ├── roles/ # role presets ├── skills/ # skills written by the server ├── notes/ # notes not tied to a workspace folder ├── run/ │ ├── agent.sock # Unix socket of the server │ ├── auth.token # token for HTTP access (mode 0600) │ ├── server.port # dynamic port of the server │ └── server.log # server output └── workspaces/<UUID>/ ├── workspace.json # nodes, connections, canvas origin and zoom, floors ├── notes/ # notes of this workspace (Markdown) ├── terminals/ # saved scrollback per terminal └── snapshots/ The format is compatible with the original Maestri. Writes are atomic (a temporary file is written and swapped in), and the file layout of workspace.json is part of that compatibility, so do not rename keys by hand. Environment variables # For you # Variable Effect OPEN_MAESTRI_DATA_DIR Use another data directory. The right way to try Maestrix, or to run tests, without touching your real data. MAESTRI_SERVER_PORT Force the port the interface connects to. Normally not needed: the port is read from run/server.port . MAESTRI_AUTH_TOKEN Override the token otherwise read from run/auth.token . OMAESTRI_PATH Path of the omaestri binary to expose inside terminals. OPEN_MAESTRI_SSH_CONFIG Alternate ssh config for the host list (tests). d: How to contribute, report problems, and who built what Maestrix is based on.
x: Contributing # Contributions are welcome. Start with CONTRIBUTING.md and, for architecture notes written for coding agents, CLAUDE.md and docs/index.md in the repository. Practical advice: Open an issue first for anything larger than a small fix. Keep pull requests focused, and add a regression test for every bug you fix. Run the Swift and Python tests before opening a PR, and run GUI tests only under Xvfb. Report security problems privately, following SECURITY.md . Roadmap # Planned work and focus areas are tracked in docs/roadmap.md . Known gaps on Linux today include the arrow and line drawing tools, a few of the node action buttons of the macOS app, and the second phase of Remote SSH. Credits # Euller : development and adaptation of Maestrix for Linux. OpenMaestri and its contributors : the macOS codebase and inherited features, including the icon in this repository. Original Maestri : product, concept and interface reference. Libraries and dependencies keep their own licenses and attributions. License # Maestrix is distributed under the GPL-3.0-or-later . See LICENSE and NOTICE . Maestrix is an independent derivative; it is not an official release of the projects it derives from.

d: The File Tree node with Git status, and Markdown notes that live on the canvas.
x: File Tree # A File Tree node browses a folder, starting from the workspace folder by default. List and grid views, with navigation buttons, an up button and a hidden-files toggle. Git integration : the header shows the current branch with a marker when the tree is dirty. Files carry badges for modified , added , deleted , renamed , conflict and untracked , and you can open a diff. Open a file in your preferred editor ( Preferences → General → Preferred IDE ) with Ctrl + Shift + E . Right-click for file operations such as creating, renaming and deleting. The tree is also an input for agents: a selected file or folder can be sent to a connected agent as an ask . Drop a folder from your file manager onto the canvas to create a File Tree rooted there. Notes # A Note is a Markdown sticky note. Switch between Raw (editable text) and Formatted (rendered Markdown). Pick a colour from the strip at the bottom. By default a note is stored inside the workspace ( ~/.open-maestri/workspaces/<id>/notes/ ). A note can also be backed by an existing file: drop a text or Markdown file on the canvas. Connected agents read and write notes with omaestri note , which makes notes a convenient shared memory between agents. See Agent communication . Portals # A Portal is an embedded web view. Use it to keep a running app, documentation or a dashboard next to the agents. Connected agents can drive it with omaestri portal … ; see the CLI reference .

d: Isolated git worktrees for each task, with hooks, and how to land the work back.
x: A floor is an isolated copy of your repository, created as a git worktree on its own branch. Terminals started inside a floor work on that branch only, so several agents can change the same project at once without stepping on each other. The Ground is the original repository. The button in the bottom-right controls shows where you are: Ground , or the name of the active floor. Needs the server Floors are driven by the server. In Standalone mode the button is disabled. See Troubleshooting . Create a floor # Click the Ground button and choose New Floor… . Type a name. The branch name is filled in as floor/<name> , and you can change it. Create. A worktree is added and terminals you open inside it start in that folder. The floor popover lists Ground and every floor. Right-click a floor to rename it, configure its hooks, land it or delete it. Hooks # Each floor can run commands at three moments, each a list of shell commands: Phase When setup After the floor is created (install dependencies, copy .env , …) run On demand, to start the project teardown Before the floor is removed Open Configure Hooks… from the popover to edit and run them. Terminals inside a floor receive the variables MAESTRI_FLOOR_NAME and MAESTRI_FLOOR_PATH . Land # Land… brings the commits of the active floor back into the Ground repository. It is only available from a floor, never from the Ground. The dialog shows why a landing is blocked when it is (for example uncommitted changes) and lets you pick the target branch. From the CLI # omaestri floor list omaestri floor create "fix-login" [ --from PATH ] [ --branch NAME ] [ --existing-branch ] [ --partitura P ] omaestri floor land "fix-login" [ --into BRANCH ] [ --delete-branch ] [ --keep-floor ] omaestri floor delete "fix-login" [ --keep-branch ] [ --keep

d: Install Maestrix, open it for the first time and connect two agents.
x: Requirements # Ubuntu 22.04 or newer (x86_64). Other Debian-based distributions should work but are not the tested target. For the .deb package: nothing else. It ships the binaries and the Swift runtime. To build from source: Swift 6, Python 3.10+ with PyGObject, GTK 4, Cairo, VTE (GTK 4 build) and WebKitGTK. The full list is in the Linux guide . Install # Option 1: the .deb package # sudo apt install ./releases/maestrix_1.0.0_amd64.deb You can also download the package from the Releases page. Afterwards, search for Maestrix in the application menu, or run: maestrix Option 2: build from source # git clone https://github.com/Potatoyz908/Maestrix.git cd Maestrix swift build -Xswiftc -use-ld = lld ./scripts/install-desktop.sh maestrix Why -use-ld=lld ? On Linux the default linker fails to link some of the Swift targets. Passing -Xswiftc -use-ld=lld works for both swift build and swift test . The maestrix launcher starts the background server when it is not running and then opens the interface. If the server dies while the app is open, the app starts it again (at most once a minute). To build the .deb yourself: ./scripts/build-deb.sh . First run # Create a workspace. Press Ctrl + Shift + N or the + in the sidebar. Choose a name, an icon and the working folder. Add a terminal. Press T on the canvas, or Ctrl + N , or use the toolbar. In the dialog pick a preset: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, OpenCode or Shell. Add a second terminal and connect the two: select a node and press L , or drag from one node to another. Talk across the rope. In the first terminal: omaestri list omaestri ask "Terminal 2" "echo hello from the other side" omaestri list shows the terminals, notes and portals connected to the one you are in. omaestri ask types the message into the other te

d: Multi-agent AI orchestration canvas for Linux.
x: Maestrix The multi-agent AI orchestration canvas for Linux. Manage agents like a team, not a pile of terminals. Get started How it works GitHub One canvas for every agent Maestrix is not an agent. It is the workspace around the agents you already use: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, OpenCode, or a plain shell. ◧ Infinite canvas Terminals, Markdown notes, file trees, browsers, labels and drawings, joined by physics-based ropes. ›_ Real terminals VTE terminals owned by a background server, so a workspace switch never kills a running shell. ⇄ Agents talk to agents omaestri ask lets connected agents delegate and answer, with no human router in between. ♪ Maestro Mode A lead agent recruits, connects, briefs and dismisses teammates by itself. ⎇ Floors Isolated git worktrees per task, with setup, run and teardown hooks, and a Land action. ⌁ Remote SSH Open a workspace whose terminals run on a remote machine, in the folder you pick. Two terminals that are not connected cannot see each other. Read the CLI reference → Dark by default, light when you want it The interface theme follows the app icon: navy ground, a blue to purple gradient and cyan highlights. d: Open a workspace whose terminals run on a remote machine, similar to VS Code Remote-SSH.
x: A remote workspace is a workspace whose terminals run on another machine, inside a folder you choose there. Maestrix connects with the system ssh , so your keys, agent and ~/.ssh/config work as usual. Phase A The first phase is delivered: host list, connection test, remote folder browser and remote terminals. The reverse tunnel, the omaestri CLI on the remote host, and a remote File Tree are not implemented yet. That means agents running on the remote machine cannot use omaestri there for now. The design is in docs/linux-ssh-spec.md . Connect # Open Connect to Host… from the + menu of the sidebar, the File menu or the Add menu. Pick a host. The list comes from your ~/.ssh/config (patterns with * or ? are skipped). Or choose Add New SSH Host… and enter user@host[:port] and, optionally, an identity file. Press Test connection . It runs ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=8 … true . If a key or password is needed, Maestrix tells you the password will be asked in the terminal. Choose the remote folder: type a path or browse (double-click to enter, Up , Home ). If the host needs a password, only the text field is available. Press Open . The workspace is created and marked with a network badge and user@host in the sidebar. How terminals start # A remote terminal runs ssh -tt to the host with a shared connection ( ControlMaster , kept for 10 minutes), then cd <folder> and your login shell, or the command you configured. There is no local shell. Password and passphrase prompts appear in the terminal itself, so nothing is stored or logged. Safety # Host, user, port and identity file are validated before any command is built: a host or user may only contain letters, digits and ._@:- and never starts with - , the port must be 1 to 65535, and the identity file must exist. d: Schedule prompts for agents and save or reapply a whole arrangement of agents.
x: Routines # A routine is a command or prompt sent to a terminal on a schedule: a recurring check, a reminder, a nightly task. Routines live in ~/.open-maestri/routines.json and run while the server is up. omaestri routine list omaestri routine show "Standup" omaestri routine create "Standup" --command "summarize yesterday's commits" --every 30m --terminal "Planner" [ --disabled ] omaestri routine edit "Standup" [ --name "New" ] [ --command "..." ] [ --every 1h ] [ --terminal "Name" ] omaestri routine enable | disable | run | delete "Standup" # run = run it now --every accepts 45s , 30m , 2h , 1h30m or a bare number of minutes. The routine manager window in the app lists, pauses, resumes and runs routines too. Before delivering a prompt the scheduler waits for the target agent to be idle. Partituras # A partitura is a saved arrangement: the agents on the canvas, their roles and their connections. Save the team that works well for one kind of task and apply it again in any workspace. omaestri partitura list omaestri partitura create "Review team" [ "Agent" ... ] # save you and your team (alias: save) omaestri partitura update "Review team" [ "Agent" ... ] omaestri partitura insert "Review team" [ --workspace W ] [ --at X,Y ] # alias: apply omaestri partitura delete "Review team" create saves the calling terminal and the agents connected to it, or the agents you name. Workspace commands # Agents can also manage workspaces: omaestri workspace list omaestri workspace create "New project" --dir ~/code/new-project omaestri workspace rename "New project" "Project" omaestri workspace move "Project" --group "Group name" # or --root omaestri workspace unload "Project"

d: Presets, roles, unique names, activity indicators and how an agent resumes its last conversation.
x: Terminals are real PTYs owned by the Maestrix server and displayed with VTE. You can run any command, and Maestrix adds agent-aware features on top. Presets # The New Terminal dialog offers one-click presets: Preset Command Claude Code claude Codex codex Gemini CLI gemini Antigravity agy --dangerously-skip-permissions OpenCode opencode Shell bash Each terminal also has a name, a command, a working directory, an icon and a colour, an activity monitor toggle and the Maestro toggle (see Maestro Mode ). Presets live in ~/.open-maestri/preferences.json and can be edited in Preferences → Agents . Skipping permission prompts The Antigravity preset starts agy with --dangerously-skip-permissions , so the agent runs tools without asking. Edit the preset if you want prompts back. Roles # A role is a named block of instructions that is injected into an agent as system context. Pick one in the dialog ( Lead , Coder , Reviewer , Tester and your own), or manage them from the CLI with omaestri role … ( CLI reference ). Unique names # omaestri ask "Name" … addresses terminals by name, so names must be unique inside a workspace (comparison ignores case): Creating or renaming a terminal to a name that is already used turns it into Name #2 , Name #3 , and so on. When a saved workspace already contains duplicates, they are renumbered Name #1 , Name #2 when it opens, and the result is saved. Activity and history # A small indicator on each node shows whether an agent is running or idle. Agent idle detection is what lets omaestri ask know when a reply is complete. The screen of every terminal is kept by the server and replayed when the interface reconnects, including full-screen programs. Switching workspaces keeps shells running. Closing a node with its × button (or Delete ) ends its shell.

d: Offline mode, missing servers, agents that cannot reach each other and other common problems.
h: omaestri: only available inside open-maestri terminals
An agent opens with an empty chat
The build fails at link time
The theme looks different from the screenshots
x: The header says "Standalone" # Standalone means the interface cannot reach the server. In that state: the Ground / Floors button is disabled and clicking it does nothing, terminals are plain local shells without MAESTRI_SOCKET , so omaestri fails inside them, leaving a workspace ends its local shells. What to do: Open Maestrix with the maestrix launcher (or from the application menu), not by running app.py directly. The launcher starts the server and exports what the app needs to restart it. Check that a server is running: pgrep -a open-maestri-server , and that ~/.open-maestri/run/server.port exists. Read the log: tail ~/.open-maestri/run/server.log . If the server died while the app was open, wait up to a minute: the app notices within seconds and restarts it when started through the launcher. Terminals created while the app was in Standalone mode stay without the variables. Close them and create new ones after the app is connected. omaestri: only available inside open-maestri terminals # You ran omaestri in a shell that Maestrix did not create, or in a terminal made in Standalone mode. Open a terminal from the canvas after the header shows Porta <number> (connected). agent 'Name' not found # The terminals are not connected, or the name differs. Run omaestri list in the calling terminal and use the name exactly as printed. Names are unique per workspace, so a duplicate may have become Name #2 . A Maestro does not recruit # The terminal must have the Maestro toggle on. Otherwise commands answer "this terminal is not in Maestro mode" . If you also have the official Maestri skills installed, the agent may follow those and call maestri instead of omaestri . Tell the agent to use omaestri or "$MAESTRI_CLI" .
